item.text: {"actions":[{"action":"Expire and remove records after at most five minutes.","mechanism":"Enforce a fixed deadline rather than extending freshness on access.","implementation":"Set expires_at using a monotonic clock when a successful source response is accepted, capped at 300 seconds. Check the deadline before serving; delete expired entries immediately. Schedule deadline-based deletion even without reads. Never renew the deadline on hits or failed fetches.","check":"With a fake clock, verify a record is unavailable at its deadline, repeated hits do not extend it, and an outage does not preserve expired entries.","risk":"Process pauses can delay physical cleanup; read-time checks must still prevent expired responses."},{"action":"Enforce the 100-record memory limit during fetches as well as caching.","mechanism":"Reserve bounded record slots before admitting source responses.","implementation":"Use a shared pool of 100 slots covering cached records and in-flight record buffers. Under an atomic admission operation, remove expired entries first, then evict the least-recently-used unreserved entry if needed. Reject admission when all slots are reserved. Release reservations on every failure path.","check":"Run concurrent misses, cancellations, and timeouts; assert occupied plus reserved slots never exceed 100 and all failed requests release reservations.","risk":"Counting only cache entries would miss temporary decoding copies; the implementation must account for these too."},{"action":"Return an explicit unavailable response when the source times out.","mechanism":"Bound waiting and separate source failure from record absence.","implementation":"Set a configurable source timeout within the request deadline. Serve an existing unexpired record without contacting the source. On a miss or expired entry, attempt the fetch; on timeout return HTTP 503 with a stable source_timeout code. Remove expired entries, retain unrelated unexpired entries, and never cache the failure as a record.","check":"Simulate a hanging source: misses return 503 within the configured deadline, valid hits still work, and expired records are neither returned nor retained.","risk":"A timeout that is too short can reject source requests that would otherwise succeed."},{"action":"Share concurrent fetches for the same record.","mechanism":"Use a bounded per-key in-flight operation instead of duplicate source calls.","implementation":"After a cache miss, atomically join or create a fetch keyed by the canonical public record identifier. Share its validated result or failure with waiting requests. Give waiters independent deadlines; cancel the shared fetch only when no waiters remain or its own deadline expires. Remove in-flight metadata on every completion path.","check":"Send concurrent requests for one missing key; verify one source call, consistent timeout responses, and no abandoned in-flight entry.","risk":"Incorrect key normalization can merge distinct records; slow waiters must not retain record buffers indefinitely."},{"action":"Pause source calls during a sustained outage.","mechanism":"Use a circuit breaker with limited recovery probes.","implementation":"Configure a failure threshold and cooldown for source timeouts and availability failures. While open, serve only unexpired cache hits and return 503 source_unavailable for misses; continue ordinary expiration and eviction. After cooldown, allow one probe. Close on success or reopen on failure. Do not count legitimate not-found responses as outages.","check":"Inject enough failures to open the breaker; verify misses stop calling the source, expired entries disappear, and only one recovery probe runs concurrently.","risk":"An overly broad breaker can block healthy source operations; scope it to the actual failure boundary."},{"action":"Reject private or unexpected fields before admitting a record.","mechanism":"Make public-data eligibility an explicit schema boundary.","implementation":"Restrict fetches to an approved public endpoint and identifier format. Validate source responses against a public-field allowlist before cache insertion; reject unexpected fields rather than caching raw responses. Disable response-body logging, tracing, and disk spill. Use synthetic records for tests and return a non-cacheable upstream-data error on validation failure.","check":"Inject an unexpected private field; verify rejection and its absence from cache, logs, traces, and client responses.","risk":"Validation cannot guarantee the source never sends private bytes; the endpoint's public-only contract is also necessary."},{"action":"Prevent obsolete fetches from repopulating invalidated records.","mechanism":"Fence asynchronous completions with slot generations.","implementation":"Assign each reserved cache slot a generation. Increment it whenever the slot is invalidated, cancelled, or reassigned. Accept a source result only if its reservation and generation still match; otherwise discard it without caching. A failed or obsolete completion must not reset any expiration deadline.","check":"Delay a fetch, invalidate and reuse its slot, then release the old response; verify it cannot overwrite the replacement or consume an additional slot.","risk":"Every insertion and invalidation path must enforce the same generation check."}],"abstention_reason":""}
